clues: This condition was first described by physician Jacob Mendes Da Costa in 1871 during the American Civil War. It frequently affected young soldiers and was sometimes known as De Costa syndrome around that time

The modern name of this syndrome came in 1982 and was formally defined by the Mayo Clinic in 1993. It can sometimes be triggered by viral or immune-system events and data shows that diagnoses of this disease increased 2-5 fold post-COVID 19 pandemic. This helped it gain a distinct ICD-10 code in 2022.
This is a disorder of the autonomic nervous system where people experience a sustained heart rate increase upon standing.

In a 2020 study, scientists screened an extensive library of existing, off-patent drugs to see if any could combat aging. They discovered that this drug significantly extends the lifespan of wild-type C. elegans otherwise known as the roundworm through activating the mitochondrial repair pathway.

Though this drug behaves similarly to thiazide diuretics, it is technically classified as a quinazoline-sulfonamide. Unlike true thiazides that lose effectiveness as the patient's kidney function drops, this drug maintains its potency even in advanced chronic kidney disease.

In the mid-20th century, the discovery of powerful loop diuretics revolutionized the treatment of severe fluid retention. However, doctors quickly ran into a major obstacle where a patient’s kidneys adapt to loop diuretics and stop responding. The introduction of this drug provided a major clinical breakthrough, as its unique chemical structure allowed it to be paired sequentially with loop diuretics to break through this resistance and safely restart fluid removal

Scientific research took off in the 1920s when UC Berkeley researcher Herbert McLean Evans injected rats with crude extract from this, turning them into giants, then shrank them back down by removing the structure.

Galen of Pergamon theorized that this was a drainage basin for the brain. He believed that waste products flowed through and this structure helped drip snot into the back of the throat or nose. This theory was not debunked until the 17th century.

In 1886, French physician Pierre Marie first linked the disorder acromegaly to this structure and in a twist of fate, Marie later developed and died from the disease himself. Other disorders caused by this gland include prolactinomas or Cushing's Disease
The word 'bougie' comes from the French word for candle. In 1801, the French surgeon Alexis Boyer performed the first formal bougienage using a tapered wax candle to treat this condition

In the late 19th and 20th centuries, accidental ingestion of houshold lye was the leading cause of these, particularly in children. American laryngologist Chevalier Jackson campaigned tirelessly for decades to pass the Federal Caustic Posion Act of 1927 which forced manufacturers to put warning labels on household chemicals
Most causes of this condition today are a result of chronic GERD. Symptoms can range from being asymptomatic to causing dyspheagia or a food impaction.

In 1841, Hungarian physician isolated the causal organism while working in Paris. Because modern petri dishes and agar did not exist yet, he used slices of potato to culture the organism and then successfully inoculated healthy tissue to recreate the disease. This marked the birth of medical mycology

In 1904, French dermatologist Raymond Sabouraud popularized using X-rays to make infected scalp hair fall out. Over the next 50 years, roughly 200,000 children worldwide, including thousands in the United States, Europe, and newly arrived immigrant children in Israel during the 1950s, had their scalps irradiated. While the x-rays cured the disease, it caused permanent baldness in many patients and led to a spike in subsequent cancers

Ancient Romans used a Latin word to describe the larvae of clothes moths. Physicians noticed that the circular, scaly patches on human skin looked remarkably similar to the round holes moth larvae chewed into woolen garments which led to this conditions' name. It can commonly affect the scalp, groin or feet leading to capitis, cruris, or pedis versions.
